# apim_mcp_proxy (Resource)

McpProxy Resource

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "github_mcp_token" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

# PROXY mode: one upstream MCP server fronted whole.
resource "apim_mcp_proxy" "github" {
  hrid         = "github-mcp"
  entity_id    = "mcp-proxy.github"
  name         = "GitHub MCP"
  context_path = "/mcp/github"
  mode         = "PROXY"
  proxy = {
    server_url = "https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/"
    upstream_auth = {
      bearer = {
        token = var.github_mcp_token
      }
    }
  }
  flows = [
    {
      name = "Rate limit tool calls"
      selectors = [
        {
          mcp = {
            methods = ["tools/call"]
          }
        }
      ]
      request = [
        {
          name   = "Quota"
          policy = "rate-limit"
          # The platform reports a configuration with the policy's defaults filled in.
          # Writing them keeps the plan empty.
          configuration = jsonencode({
            errorStrategy = "FALLBACK_PASS_TROUGH"
            rate = {
              limit          = 100
              periodTime     = 1
              periodTimeUnit = "MINUTES"
              key            = ""
              useKeyOnly     = false
            }
          })
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
  plans = [
    {
      name = "Default"
      security = {
        api_key = {
          source = "HEADER"
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}

resource "apim_catalog_mcp_server" "github" {
  hrid      = "github"
  entity_id = "mcp-server.github"
  server_connection = {
    endpoint = "https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/"
    auth = {
      header = {
        name  = "Authorization"
        value = "Bearer ${var.github_mcp_token}"
      }
    }
  }
}

# STUDIO mode: tools picked from catalog MCP servers.
resource "apim_mcp_proxy" "dev-tools" {
  hrid         = "dev-tools"
  entity_id    = "mcp-proxy.dev-tools"
  name         = "Developer Tools"
  context_path = "/mcp/dev-tools"
  mode         = "STUDIO"
  studio = {
    # Sorted by server, then by tool.
    tools = [
      {
        server = apim_catalog_mcp_server.github.hrid
        tool   = "create_issue"
      },
      {
        server = apim_catalog_mcp_server.github.hrid
        tool   = "list_pull_requests"
        alias  = "list_prs"
      }
    ]
    # One entry per server a tool comes from.
    upstream_auth = [
      {
        server = apim_catalog_mcp_server.github.hrid
        auth = {
          bearer = {
            token = var.github_mcp_token
          }
        }
      }
    ]
    enable_fga = true
  }
  plans = [
    {
      name = "Default"
      security = {
        api_key = {
          source = "HEADER"
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `context_path` (String) Context path the gateway serves the proxy on; must be available in the environment
- `entity_id` (String) Stable identity of the proxy, the name authorization policies reference: lowercase, dot-separated
segments, first segment `mcp-proxy`. Required. Validated,
never repaired: an invalid value, or a value already used by another MCP proxy of the environment, is
rejected. Immutable once the proxy exists — declaring a different value is rejected rather than
applied. Delete the proxy and declare it again to give it another identity. Uniqueness across the
environment is checked at apply time, not enforced by the store (AIAM-242): two concurrent applies
of the same entityId can both pass.
- `hrid` (String) A unique human readable id identifying this resource. Requires replacement if changed.
- `mode` (String) Shape of the proxy, and the one block it carries: `PROXY` fronts one upstream MCP server, declared under
`proxy`; `STUDIO` composes a curated tool surface out of catalog MCP servers, declared under `studio`. The
other mode's block is rejected. Required. Fixed at creation: declaring another mode on
an existing proxy is rejected, and changing it is a delete and a new declaration.
must be one of ["PROXY", "STUDIO"]
- `name` (String) Display name of the proxy; converges on re-apply
- `plans` (Attributes List) Plans consumers subscribe to, converged by name: a declared plan the proxy does not have is created
and published, a plan the proxy holds in staging is published, a plan the declaration no longer
carries is closed — closing terminates its subscriptions — and a plan cannot be changed in place
under the same name. At least one plan is required. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--plans))

### Optional

- `description` (String) Human description of the proxy; converges on re-apply
- `environment_id` (String) environment ID
- `flow_execution` (Attributes) How the gateway selects among the proxy's flows. `DEFAULT` runs every flow whose selectors match;
`BEST_MATCH` runs the one whose selectors match best. Omitted, APIM's defaults apply and the state
reports no execution block. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--flow_execution))
- `flows` (Attributes List) Policy flows of the proxy, in execution order, run after the flows of the plan the request matched.
The manifest owns them: on every apply the proxy's flows are replaced by the declared ones, so a
flow authored in the policy studio survives only if the manifest carries it, and omitting `flows`
removes them all. Each step's configuration is validated against its policy's schema, on apply and
on dry run, and reported back as stored. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--flows))
- `identity_providers` (Attributes List) Authorization servers declared on the proxy as OAuth2 resources, which OAUTH2 plans reference through
`provider`. Converged by name: a declared provider the proxy lacks is attached; a declared provider
whose configuration differs from the proxy's resource is rejected, except a generic provider's
`clientSecret`, which replaces the stored one when it differs and is kept when omitted; a resource
no longer declared is left in place; a declared provider named like a resource the proxy holds
disabled, or under another type, is rejected. At most one `GRAVITEE_AM` provider, provisioned when
the proxy is created only. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--identity_providers))
- `organization_id` (String) organization ID
- `proxy` (Attributes) What a `PROXY` fronts: one upstream MCP server and the credential the gateway presents to it. Required when
`mode` is `PROXY`, rejected otherwise. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--proxy))
- `state` (String) Lifecycle of the proxy on the gateway. `STARTED` runs it with the last applied definition and redeploys it
after every apply that changes it; `STOPPED` makes the gateway answer 404 and stores changes without
deploying them, which the next `STARTED` does. `STARTED` when omitted. Reported back as the lifecycle APIM
observes. A start or a deploy the gateway side refuses fails the apply with a `500` carrying the technical
code `gamma.mcp.lifecycle.failed` and the operation, the proxy and the cause as parameters; the declaration
is stored, and the next apply starts the proxy or redeploys the one APIM reports out of sync.
Default: "STARTED"; must be one of ["STARTED", "STOPPED"]
- `studio` (Attributes) What a `STUDIO` exposes: tools picked from catalog MCP servers of the environment, the credential the
gateway presents to each of those servers, and whether the platform's fine-grained authorization runs on
tool calls. Tools converge as a set — adding, removing or re-aliasing one replaces the studio's tool
surface — and `upstreamAuth` converges per server. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--studio))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Resource UUID

Optional:

matched. Owned by the manifest like the proxy's flows, and — unlike `security` — free to change in

- `name` (String) Name of the plan, the key plan convergence matches on. Not Null
- `security` (Attributes) How consumers authenticate against the plan, discriminated by `type`. Not Null (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--plans--security))

<a id="nestedatt--proxy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `proxy`

Required:

- `server_url` (String) URL of the upstream MCP server, http or https; the gateway reaches it at runtime

Optional:

- `upstream_auth` (Attributes) Authentication the gateway uses against the upstream MCP server, discriminated by `type`. Credential values
are stored verbatim: a literal, or a `secret://` URI pointing at a configured secret provider. They are
never returned by this API. Omitting `proxy.upstreamAuth`, or declaring `type: NONE`, means the gateway passes
the caller's credentials through — and clears any stored upstream authentication. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--proxy--upstream_auth))

<a id="nestedatt--studio"></a>
### Nested Schema for `studio`

Required:

- `tools` (Attributes List) The tools the studio exposes, each named by the catalog server it comes from and its runtime name.
Every server named here needs an `upstreamAuth` entry. On a studio created with a `GRAVITEE_AM`
provider, a tool added after creation is served but not registered as a scope on the Access
Management domain; the apply reports it as a warning. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--studio--tools))
- `upstream_auth` (Attributes List) One entry per catalog server a tool comes from: the credential the gateway presents to that server,
stored verbatim and never returned, or `type: NONE` to say the server needs none. Nothing is inferred
from the credential the catalog synced the server with. An entry for a server no tool uses, a server
without an entry, or two entries for one server are rejected. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--studio--upstream_auth))

Optional:

- `enable_fga` (Boolean) Inserts the platform's fine-grained authorization flow, which runs the `authz-pep` policy on
`tools/call` with the called tool as the resource; `false` removes it. That flow belongs to the
platform: `flows` may not carry an `authz-pep` step themselves, and the state reports the declared
flows without it.
Default: false

- `server` (String) HRID of the `catalog/mcp-servers` resource of this environment the tool comes from. Not Null
- `tool` (String) Runtime name of the tool, as the server's state lists it under `tools`. Not Null

Read-Only:

- `entity_id` (String) Composed entity id of the tool, the name an authorization policy references, e.g. `mcp-tool.github.create_issue`

- `type` (String) Type of upstream authentication. Default: "NONE"; must be "NONE"


<a id="nestedatt--studio--upstream_auth--auth--oauth2"></a>
### Nested Schema for `studio.upstream_auth.auth.oauth2`

Required:

- `authorize_url` (String) Authorization endpoint the elicitation flow sends the user to
- `client_id` (String) Client id of the upstream OAuth 2.0 client
- `client_secret` (String, Sensitive) Client secret of the upstream OAuth 2.0 client, a literal or a `secret://` URI stored verbatim; never returned
- `token_url` (String) Token endpoint the gateway exchanges the authorization code at

Optional:

- `scopes` (List of String) Scopes requested with the token
- `type` (String) Type of upstream authentication. Default: "OAUTH2"; must be "OAUTH2"

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = apim_mcp_proxy.github
  id = jsonencode({
    environment_id  = "DEFAULT"
    hrid            = "github-mcp"
    organization_id = "DEFAULT"
  })
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import apim_mcp_proxy.github '{"environment_id": "DEFAULT", "hrid": "github-mcp", "organization_id": "DEFAULT"}'
```
